Truth fix: a delay variable or guard expression is found as a whole name in code, not as a substring of
any raw line. bash bound z to the "// zero" comment of line 3 (false literal-zero), took the commented-out
Math.max(d, 1L) of line 5 as the floor of d (false clean) and let "delayw > 0" guard w (false PASS).
-- args --
@DIR@/t
-- want --
exit 1
FAIL  lint-delays     @DIR@/t/B.java:4  unfloored  cannot verify floor of variable: z
FAIL  lint-delays     @DIR@/t/B.java:6  unfloored  cannot verify floor of variable: d
FAIL  lint-delays     @DIR@/t/B.java:8  unfloored  cannot verify floor of variable: w
-- stderr --
-- t/B.java --
class B {
  void a(long z, long d, long w) {
    foo(BRelTime.make(0)); // zero delay elsewhere
    Clock.schedule(this, BRelTime.make(z), go, null);
    // d = Math.max(d, 1L) was here
    Clock.schedule(this, BRelTime.make(d), go, null);
    if (delayw > 0) foo();
    Clock.schedule(this, BRelTime.make(w), go, null);
    long n = Math.max(w, 1L);
    Clock.schedule(this, BRelTime.make(n), go, null);
    if (this.w > 0) Clock.schedule(this, BRelTime.make(n), go, null);
  }
}
